subject: Monitor log-likelihood in Stan for NLMM with left-censoring data

messages.author: 53d479b609cc8ad3
messages.subject: Monitor log-likelihood in Stan for NLMM with left-censoring data
parts:
Hi,
I fitted a Non-Linear Mixed Model (NLMM) in Stan:
The model has 4 random effects: A0 is assumed to have a log-normal distribution so A0,i = A0*exp(bi) where bi ~ Normal(0, sigma_A0).
beta, gamma and alpha are assumed to have normal distributions, so, for example: beta,i = beta + bbeta,i where bbetai ~ Normal(0, sigma_beta).
There is one covariate: C2 (1 if child2, 0 if child0).
The model is successfully implemented in Stan.

Now I want to test GOF for the distribution specified for the response (I assumed the data are normal on log10 scale), more specifically for the left-censoring data points using the method proposed by Nysen R. et al. (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/22714389).
After some calculation, the likelihood turns out to be a little bit complicated since it is involved the extended term, the term in density of a normal distribution: exp(-(y-mu)^2/2) and the cumulative distribution function of a standard normal.
For example, with extended model r = 2, I have the likelihood for:
 - Non censoring data:
    target += 1/sigma * phiz[i] * (a0^2 + 2*a0*a1*diff[i] + a1^2*(diff[i])^2)
 - Censoring data:
   target += (a1^2 + a0^2)*exp(normal_lcdf(y[i] | mu[i], sigma)) - 2*a0*a1*phiz[i] - diff[i]*a1^2*phiz[i]
where
   phiz = exp(-((y-mu)/sigma)^2/2);
   diff = (y-mu)/sigma;
These are for easy parameterization of the model.
I noticed that normal_lcdf would return the log of the cumulative distribution, so I put it into the exp() to calculate the true value.  Later one, in the generated quantities, I put all again in a log statement.  
The mu  is time-dependent and it is calculated in the transformed parameters block.
transformed parameters{
     vector[J] b;
     real betapart[N];
     real gammapart[N];
     real alphapart[N];
     real A0part[N];
     real a0;
     real a1;
     real diff[N];
     real<lower=0> phiz[N];
     real mu[N];

     a0 = sin(phi1);
     a1 = cos(phi1)*sin(phi2);
     b = sigma_A0*b_raw;
     for (i in 1:N) {
     A0part[i]    = b[subj[i]] +vA0*C2[i];
     betapart[i] = beta + bbeta[subj[i]] + vbeta*C2[i];
     gammapart[i] = gamma + bgamma[subj[i]] +vgamma*C2[i];
     alphapart[i] = alpha  + balpha[subj[i]] +valpha*C2[i]; }

     // The mean
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( time[i] <= 2 ) {
            mu[i]  = log10(A0*exp(A0part[i] -betapart[i]*time[i])) ; }
        else if ( time[i] >2 && time[i] <=h ) {
            mu[i] = log10(A0*exp(A0part[i] -2*betapart[i] + gammapart[i]*(time[i]-2) ) ) ; }
       else if ( time[i] > h ) {
            mu[i] = log10(A0*exp(A0part[i] - 2*betapart[i] + gammapart[i]*(h-2) -alphapart[i]*(time[i]-h)) );}
     // Calculate (ynew-mu)/sigma and exp(-1/2*(ynew - mu)^2/ sigma^2)
     diff[i] = (y[i] - mu[i])/sigma;
     phiz[i] = (1/sqrt(2*pi())) * exp(-(diff[i])^2/2);
     }

}Enter code here...


I monitor the log-likelihood by using the log-lik put in the generated quantities block.
generated quantities {
     vector[N] pre;
     vector[N] log_lik;
     real ll;
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( cens[i] ==0 ) {
            pre[i] = 1/sigma * phiz[i] * (a0^2 + 2*a0*a1*diff[i] + a1^2*(diff[i])^2);
            log_lik[i] = log(pre[i]);}
        else if ( cens[i] ==1 ) {
            pre[i] = (a1^2 + a0^2)*exp(normal_lcdf(y[i] | mu[i], sigma)) - 2*a0*a1*phiz[i] - diff[i]*a1^2*phiz[i];
            log_lik[i] = log(pre[i]);}
     }
}


But when I called the command:  to extract the log-likelihood, there are some warnings:
   
the following parameters were dropped because they are constant
log_lik[13] log_lik[19] log_lik[28] log_lik[37] log_lik[50] log_lik[76] log_lik[79] log_lik[86] log_lik[92] log_lik[114] log_lik[128] log_lik[153] log_lik[160] log_lik[180] log_lik[183] log_lik[191] log_lik[198] log_lik[204] log_lik[222] log_lik[225] log_lik[248] log_lik[252] log_lik[255] log_lik[278] log_lik[284] log_lik[285] log_lik[294]
the following parameters were dropped because they are duplicative
log_lik[59] log_lik[84] log_lik[102] log_lik[105] log_lik[108] log_lik[127] log_lik[195] log_lik[208] log_lik[214] log_lik[242] log_lik[267] log_lik[271] log_lik[274] log_lik[297]
which are corresponding to the log-likelihood of left-cenosring data points.

Could any one help a hand on it and point out what is going wrong here?
Many thanks.



Here are the whole code:
child   <- read.csv('data_childcens_4Cov27Jun16.csv', sep = ",", dec='.', header=T, na.strings = '.'); head(child)
str(child)
child$ID<- paste("A", child$id, sep = ""); child$ID <- as.factor(child$ID); str(child)
N       <- nrow(child); N                                                      #302
cens    <- subset(child, CENS ==1 & t > 4); str(cens)
# Recode for kind as binary variable 0,1.
child$C2<- NULL; child$C2[child$kind == "C1"] <- 0; child$C2[child$kind == "C2"] <- 1
# Recode for AB_Mum2 as binary variable 0,1.
child$ABMum <- NULL; child$ABMum[child$AB_Mum2 == "Less"] <- 0; child$ABMum[child$AB_Mum2 == "More"] <- 1


#-------------------- Data for Stan - Model with and without covariate
stan_dat<- list(subj = as.integer(child$ID),
           N    = N,
           J    = nlevels(child$ID),
           y    = child$y_new,
           time = child$t,
           cens = child$CENS,
           C2   = child$C2,
           ABMum= child$ABMum)

model_ex2 <- "
data {
     int<lower=1> N;                         // Total number of data points
     real<lower=0> time[N];                  // Time points
     real<lower=0> y[N];                     // Antibody levels on log10 scale
     int<lower=1>     J;                     // Number of subjects
     int<lower=1, upper=J>    subj[N];       // Subject id
     int<lower=0, upper=1>    cens[N];       // Censoring indication
     int<lower=0, upper=1>    C2[N];         // Child indication
}

parameters {
     real<lower=0> beta;
     real<lower=0> gamma;
     real<lower=4> h;
     real<lower=0> alpha;
     real<lower=0> A0;

     vector[J] b_raw;                          //To apply non-centered parameterization
     vector[J] bbeta;
     vector[J] bgamma;
     vector[J] balpha;

     real<lower=0> sigma_A0;
     real<lower=0> sigma;
     real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
     real<lower=0> sigma_gamma;
     real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;

     real vA0;
     real vbeta;
     real vgamma;
     real valpha;

     real<lower=-pi()/2, upper=pi()/2> phi1;
     real<lower=-pi()/2, upper=pi()/2> phi2;
}

transformed parameters{
     vector[J] b;
     real betapart[N];
     real gammapart[N];
     real alphapart[N];
     real A0part[N];
     real a0;
     real a1;
     real diff[N];
     real<lower=0> phiz[N];
     real mu[N];

     a0 = sin(phi1);
     a1 = cos(phi1)*sin(phi2);
     b = sigma_A0*b_raw;
     for (i in 1:N) {
     A0part[i]    = b[subj[i]] +vA0*C2[i];
     betapart[i] = beta + bbeta[subj[i]] + vbeta*C2[i];
     gammapart[i] = gamma + bgamma[subj[i]] +vgamma*C2[i];
     alphapart[i] = alpha  + balpha[subj[i]] +valpha*C2[i]; }

     // The mean
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( time[i] <= 2 ) {
            mu[i]  = log10(A0*exp(A0part[i] -betapart[i]*time[i])) ; }
        else if ( time[i] >2 && time[i] <=h ) {
            mu[i] = log10(A0*exp(A0part[i] -2*betapart[i] + gammapart[i]*(time[i]-2) ) ) ; }
       else if ( time[i] > h ) {
            mu[i] = log10(A0*exp(A0part[i] - 2*betapart[i] + gammapart[i]*(h-2) -alphapart[i]*(time[i]-h)) );}
     // Calculate (ynew-mu)/sigma and exp(-1/2*(ynew - mu)^2/ sigma^2)
     diff[i] = (y[i] - mu[i])/sigma;
     phiz[i] = (1/sqrt(2*pi())) * exp(-(diff[i])^2/2);
     }

}
model {
     // Priors
     b_raw ~ normal(0, 1);                    //subj random effects - As we apply non-centered parameterization
     bbeta ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
     bgamma~ normal(0, sigma_gamma);
     balpha~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
     // Likelihood
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( cens[i] ==0 ) {
            target += 1/sigma * phiz[i] * (a0^2 + 2*a0*a1*diff[i] + a1^2*(diff[i])^2) ; }
        else if ( cens[i] ==1 ) {
            target += (a1^2 + a0^2)*exp(normal_lcdf(y[i] | mu[i], sigma)) - 2*a0*a1*phiz[i] - diff[i]*a1^2*phiz[i]   ;  }
             }
}

generated quantities {
     vector[N] pre;
     vector[N] log_lik;
     real ll;
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( cens[i] ==0 ) {
            pre[i] = 1/sigma * phiz[i] * (a0^2 + 2*a0*a1*diff[i] + a1^2*(diff[i])^2);
            log_lik[i] = log(pre[i]);}
        else if ( cens[i] ==1 ) {
            pre[i] = (a1^2 + a0^2)*exp(normal_lcdf(y[i] | mu[i], sigma)) - 2*a0*a1*phiz[i] - diff[i]*a1^2*phiz[i];
            log_lik[i] = log(pre[i]);}
     }
}
"

#------------------- Running model in STAN
ex2 <- stan(model_code=model_ex2, data=stan_dat, pars=c('A0','beta','gamma','alpha','h', 'phi1','phi2','log_lik',
                                                                   'sigma','sigma_A0','sigma_beta','sigma_gamma','sigma_alpha',
                                                                   'vA0', 'vbeta', 'vgamma', 'valpha'),
                    chains=1, iter=5000, warmup=2500,
                    control=list(adapt_delta=0.99, stepsize = 0.01, max_treedepth =15))

There's nothing wrong with the expression per se if all the values are finite.
But exponentiating a log CDF can quickly lead to underflow and given that
the target density is on the log scale, this usually is not the right thing
to do.

Hi Bob,
Thank you.
However, my likelihood is something like I put above.
So I really want to have the value of the cumulative distribution function on original scale, but not on the log scale. The same thing for the density function of normal distribution.
For the density function, I could write it down by something like: 1/sqrt(2pi *sigma) * exp(-(y-mu)^2/2).
But for the cumulative distribution function, since I have read that Stan does not have integrate() function, so I can only use the normal_lcdf()  command, which produces the value of cumulative distribution function  on log scale (Link: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-3-Density-Notation-and-Increments).
So as long as if everything that I understand is correct, it should not be wrong to use: exp(normal_lcdf(y | mu, sigma)).
Hope I made myself clear.


       








  
And when I look into the Stan manual

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Monitor log-likelihood in Stan for NLMM with left-censoring data
parts:
Stan assumes the models are programmed on the log scale.
So you want to code the log likelihood, not the likelihood.

So when you apply log() and then use log_sum_exp on the additive
terms, you'll wind up needing the log-scale CDFs.

Not that our log-scale CDFs are particularly robust. They're
pretty much coded up as the log of the CDF pending help from
a numerical analyst who can write good log CDF and derivatives
for us!

- Bob

> For the density function, I could write it down by something like: 1/sqrt(2pi *sigma) * exp(-(y-mu)^2/2).
> But for the cumulative distribution function, since I have read that Stan does not have integrate() function, so I can only use the normal_lcdf() command, which produces the value of cumulative distribution function on log scale (Link: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-3-Density-Notation-and-Increments).
> So as long as if everything that I understand is correct, it should not be wrong to use: exp(normal_lcdf(y | mu, sigma)).

messages.author: 53d479b609cc8ad3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Monitor log-likelihood in Stan for NLMM with left-censoring data
parts:
Only for updated purpose:

Thank you Bob for your patience.
The problem is finally solved. I should use normal_cdf() instead of using exp(normal_lcdf()).
The final code working well is:

generated quantities {

vector[N] log_lik;
     real ll;
     for (i in 1:N){
        if ( cens[i] ==0 ) {
log_lik[i] = log(pre[i])-log(sigma) -log(sqrt(2*pi())) -(diff[i])^2 + log(a0^2 + 2*a0*a1*diff[i] + a1^2*(diff[i])^2);}
else if ( cens[i] ==1 ) {

log_lik[i] = log((a1^2 + a0^2)*normal_cdf(diff[i], 0, 1) - 2*a0*a1*phiz[i] - diff[i]*a1^2*phiz[i]);}
     }
}

Thao.
